claims.text: Near-equiatomic compositions have high configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy stabilizes simple solid-solution phases over intermetallic formation or phase segregation.
Severe lattice distortion lowers atomic diffusivity in high-entropy alloys.
High configurational entropy forces severe lattice distortions.
Near-equiatomic, single-phase nanoparticles remain chemically and structurally stable throughout catalytic temperatures of 773–1173 K and thermoelectric temperatures of 473–1923 K.
Chemical disorder produces a high density of atomic-scale defects in the nanoparticles.
Local lattice distortions and atomic-scale defects kinetically trap atoms in a disordered single-phase structure.
Suppressed atomic diffusion prevents phase segregation at high temperature.
Suppressed atomic diffusion prevents nanoparticle coarsening at high temperature.
Suppressed diffusion maintains nanoparticle structural integrity and a uniform distribution of constituent elements.
Slight off-stoichiometric deviations from a near-equiatomic composition reduce configurational entropy.
After prolonged high-temperature exposure, near-equiatomic nanoparticles will retain a single-phase structure and homogeneous composition.
After identical exposure, off-stoichiometric nanoparticles will exhibit more phase decomposition and chemical segregation than near-equiatomic nanoparticles.
After identical exposure, off-stoichiometric nanoparticles will exhibit more grain growth than near-equiatomic nanoparticles.
Substantial oxidation or initial multiphase formation can overwhelm the proposed entropy-based kinetic stabilization.
